preamble: Monophthongization of the diphthong /ei/ to a mid front monophthong /e/ (often long [eː]) through absorption of the off-glide. It is a recurrent change: Attic Greek ει became [eː] before the Classical period, East Norse turned æi into ē (stæin > sten 'stone') from the 10th century, and many European Portuguese vernaculars reduce ei to [e] (queijo [ˈkeʒu]).

examples.note: The diphthongs /ei ou/ became the long monophthongs /eː oː/ before the Classical period; /ei/ remained only before vowels.

languageExamples.language: Old East Norse (Old Danish, Old Swedish)

examples.note: The monophthongization æi > ē began in mid-10th-century Denmark and is the chief feature separating Old East Norse from Old West Norse; Old Gutnish kept stain.
Optional monophthongization of ei before a palatal and before consonants, depending on speaker and region; Lisbon instead has [ɐj].
Also roupeiro [ʁoˈpeɾu], bandeira [bɐ̃ˈdeɾɐ]; final -ei (rei, lei) keeps the diphthong.
